body:
Timer was never supposed to be so complicated. :( It was supposed to work like this:
http://pastebin.com/46nwpcKM
Unfortunately, posting a runnable each frame wrecks non-continuous rendering, causing it to render each frame. There isn't really a cross platform way to avoid posted runnables triggering a render. I would say people doing non-continuous rendering can avoid just Timer, except Timer is used internally by libgdx: GestureDetector, TextField, DragScrollListener. A separate thread was introduced to try to fix this, but this increased the complexity quite a bit.

We can either fix it as you suggest (feel free to create a PR) or come up with some way to use the simpler, better postRunnable version.

Sort of related, Pools never clears the pools between runs. This doesn't hurt, just wastes memory. Maybe we need a surefire way to clean up things like this when libgdx starts, eg some static listeners libgdx runs when it starts. Maybe LifecycleListener could use an initialize method since it seems dispose isn't called reliably?
Yeah, the way dispose is called on android is not really the way to go: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/5227071/understanding-of-isfinishing
We can make sure the thread is associated with the currently running app in the Timer instance constructor. No more stupid static block. I see if i can fix it.
IMO a LifecycleListener initialize method would let Timer, Pools and other things clear out old state at startup.

Ideally I agree with @NathanSweet. However there are 2 aspects to take into consideration:
- it's a breaking API change.
- you must define where and when the create method should be invoked. I can think of two places: as soon as you add the listener (regardless of the current thread) or from inside the rendering thread on the next execution cycle.

Since the create method has no real common use (correct me if I'm wrong) and  the problem is confined to the android backend, I think you can cut to the chase and manage the cleanup when creating and disposing graphics.

I'm afraid I'm having the same problem. If I close the app for example by pressing the home button, the next time I open the app, timer is no longer working.
Is there a solution yet? Thank you very much

issue.title: Timers can be wiped out when using GestureDetector
Prevent Timers from being wiped out
issue.body: This fixes #2274 by removing Timer.checkStatics and instead implementing @suluke's suggestion in #1548 to set Timer.thread to null on pause. This should prevent the issue he reported, while also removing the possibility of internal Timer instantiations wiping out user-created Timers.
